initiative.title: Unified product workspace
initiative.summary: Turn overview, wireframe, and flow documents into connected views inside one capability-centered project workspace.

sources.anchor: turn it into a coherent single app instead of 3 smaller apps or feature sets

sources.location: Current task: response after initial proposal
Current task: annotation about project organization
sources.anchor: I expect overviews to be quite common. They make a nice summary and organizing doc.

sources.location: Current task: annotation about wireframe ownership
sources.anchor: they will nearly always be associated with a capability or in a flow somehow
Let's create a proper implementation plan. I'll review before we mint tickets.
Let's go ahead and create tickets breaking down the work.
Preserve typed diagram semantics, dependable pointer interaction, source safety, and shared diagram documentation.
Home loads the catalog and selected document, then dispatches to three full-page workbench components.
One secure catalog and document reader serve every declared diagram type.
OverviewOrigin already preserves overview, capability, and view context when a capability opens a flow.
Wireframes own screen and shot state and can embed one real overview or flow scene.
Flows can use browser-local working copies while overview refresh keeps the last valid source-backed view.
Node tests cover DSL, navigation, inventory, catalog safety, refresh, and flow behavior. Browser checks remain separate.

claims.statement: Overview, wireframe, and flow documents feel like connected views inside one application.
A common project normally starts from an overview that summarizes and organizes its capabilities.
Capability context remains visible while a person opens related screens and flows.
A wireframe can relate to a capability before a related flow exists.
Keep separate overview, wireframe, and flow models inside one workspace.
Semantic navigation comes from explicit safe references, not folder membership or inference.
Projects without overviews and artifacts without capability links remain usable and discoverable.
Do not create a universal product graph or merge the three DSL bodies.
Byron reviews the implementation plan before tickets are created.

options.premise: Files are the main project unit.
The overview is the required navigation hub.
Screens are the main product unit.
One semantic graph owns every artifact.
Capabilities connect separate typed artifacts inside one shell.

shape.appetite: One focused capability delivered through four useful milestones without replacing the current renderers or adding storage.
shape.problem: Separate page chrome and navigation make three connected document types feel like separate applications.
shape.recommended_shape: A persistent capability-centered workspace around the existing overview, wireframe, and flow renderers.
success_moves: Prove the shell with the existing overview-to-flow relationship before changing syntax.
Keep specialized renderer state with its current owner.
Add only a typed capability-to-wireframe reference.
Derive backlinks from the active overview before considering project-wide indexing.
Keep render mode and direct document URLs as bypasses.
Use the existing inventory when no overview can become the home.

first_proof.question: Does persistent project and capability context make overview and flow feel like one application?
first_proof.artifact: A local resume-project journey from overview capability to flow and back inside one workspace shell.
first_proof.decision_rule: Continue when context remains clear and flow interaction stays dependable; fall back to shared chrome when the shell harms the canvas.

rabbit_holes: Project manifest before multiple-overview behavior requires one

milestones.title: One shell preserves overview and flow context
milestones.outcome: The resume overview and linked flow work inside one persistent project shell.
milestones.proof: Browser navigation, refresh, history, render bypass, and direct flow interaction checks.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: All three document types remain usable through direct URLs and the inventory fallback.
milestones.rollback: Remove the shell wrapper and retain current conditional workbench dispatch.

milestones.title: A capability opens its wireframe screens
milestones.outcome: A capability can open a validated wireframe document and optional screen with preserved overview context.
milestones.proof: DSL round trips, secure resolver fixtures, warning repair, and an overview-to-screen browser journey.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Flow links and standalone wireframes remain valid when no wireframe reference exists.
milestones.rollback: Remove representative wireframe references and ignore the optional capability field.

milestones.title: The overview organizes project navigation
milestones.outcome: The active overview provides capability navigation while every catalog document remains discoverable.
milestones.proof: Pure projection tests plus browser checks for linked, shared, invalid, and not-linked-here documents.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: The workspace can fall back to its overview chooser and complete diagram inventory.
milestones.rollback: Hide the capability navigator and keep the shell's chooser and inventory.

milestones.title: The workspace replaces duplicate application chrome
milestones.outcome: Overview, wireframe, and flow work feel like views inside one application.
milestones.proof: Full unit, type, build, CLI capture, accessibility, and clean browser regression evidence.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Specialized renderer controls and source ownership remain intact inside shared navigation.
milestones.rollback: Restore renderer-specific chrome while keeping proven relationships and catalog behavior.
